topics.topic: Current topology decisions governing service-surface reachability
questions: Which current topology decision defines who may reach each surface, given that R0-19 is marked replaced and its host-only rule conflicts with R0-28, R0-39 and R0-48 permitting the service API over the protected inter-host WireGuard channel?
May A21 and A17 still rely on R0-19, or must they name the replacement decisions that now govern reachability?
May the renewed security review rely on R0-19's deployment rule, or must it instead cite and apply its current replacements R0-27, R0-28, R0-29, R0-39 and R0-48?

quotes:
The addresses are the deployment's, as R0-19 says
   — the host's loopback where Registry runs on the host, its internal
   network where it runs in a container — so the configuration names them
   (owner, 2026-11-11, replacing the release-fixed addresses of 2026-11-01:
   one release cannot hold both).
judgement.why: P8 already decides the same reachability-basis question on unchanged texts, assigning current network reachability to host administration under R0-28, R0-29 and R0-48.

precedent.topic: Normative reachability basis and whether Registry must enforce listener-network confinement
quotes:
Registry is one process (R0-05) serving two surfaces (Actors and trust
boundaries, "Network surface"): the service API, for the four services of A09,
and the owner interface. Which networks reach each surface, and the HTTPS that
carries the owner interface from another machine, are the host's
administration (R0-28, R0-29, R0-48; Explicit exclusions): Registry serves
each surface on a listener of its own and decides nothing about reachability.
precedent.why: State 3 bases the current topology on R0-28, R0-29 and R0-48 and expressly assigns network reachability to host administration, so Registry does not reject a syntactically valid bind address for reachability reasons.

topics.topic: Definition and enforcement of overlapping listener endpoints, including reuse options
questions: What exactly counts as an overlapping endpoint, and must Registry guarantee refusal against a later socket regardless of the later socket's reuse options and the platform's default binding rules?
What exactly counts as an overlapping endpoint: only the identical host and port, or also wildcard/specific-address pairs and other address ranges that accept some of the same connections?
Exactly which host-and-port combinations count as overlapping, particularly wildcard versus specific IPv4 addresses, wildcard versus specific IPv6 addresses, and IPv4 versus IPv6 addresses?
With which options must the second socket attempt the bind, and must the test also prove failure when that socket requests every supported address- or port-sharing option?

quotes:
Registry binds each listener
   exclusively — it sets no option that lets a second active socket bind
   an overlapping endpoint — and an IPv6 listener accepts IPv6 connections
   alone, never IPv4 ones mapped onto it; whether a port a closed listener
   left can be bound again at once is the platform's, which Registry
   neither requires nor prevents.
judgement.why: The exclusivity passage appears unchanged in the closed and reopened A17 text, and no reopening change touched it or made the endpoint-overlap question newly material.

topics.topic: Listener handoff representation for validated host addresses and ports
questions: After validation, what exact types and forms are handed to the listener: the original strings, canonical bracketless IP text, or parsed IP-address values, and is the port an integer or decimal text?
After parsing an IPv6 address, is the handed-on host the bracketed text such as `[::1]`, the unbracketed text `::1`, or a typed IP-address value, and is the port text or an integer?

quotes:
Registry's code receives each item as a field of the settings the one
   module that reads the environment loads; no other part of Registry reads
   a variable.
judgement.why: P1 already assigns the exact handed-on representation and field types to State 6, and neither the question nor its supporting passage has changed.

precedent.topic: Representation and types used to hand host and port to listener code
quotes:
Registry's code receives each item as a field of the settings the one
   module that reads the environment loads; no other part of Registry reads
   a variable.
precedent.why: Exact environment names, settings-field names, field types, diagnostic identifiers and parsed representations are configuration-schema and field-type details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Named constant or typed predicate for detecting the IPv4-mapped prefix
questions: The exclusion must name the imported data-provider constant that holds the IPv4-mapped prefix, rather than placing the prefix value directly in the design text read by generated validation code.

The IPv4-mapped prefix must either become a named imported data-provider constant used by the generated checking code, or the passage must specify a typed/library predicate that does not deliver this literal prefix to generated code.

judgement.why: The literal IPv4-mapped-prefix passage appears unchanged in the closed and reopened A17 text, and no reopening change touched it or made its value-delivery path newly material.

topics.topic: Portable witness-socket scenario required for the listener exclusivity test
questions: Which address family, bind address, socket options and actor must the witness socket use so that this test has one portable required meaning?
Which configured IPv6 address, destination address, client location, protocol and observed failure must the Required tests item use to demonstrate this rule?

quotes:
`[fe80::1%eth0]:8781`, `[::ffff:127.0.0.1]:8781`, `127.0.0.01:8781` and
   `127.0.0.1:08781` each stop the start, naming the item. While Registry
   runs, a second socket binding the service API's endpoint fails; an IPv4
   client cannot reach an IPv6 listener.
judgement.why: The required-test passage appears unchanged in the closed and reopened A17 text, and no reopening change touched it or made the witness-socket scenarios newly material.

topics.topic: Security-review categories and references required for exclusive binding
questions: Must the new exclusive-binding behavior and its competing-socket case also reopen the concurrency category and add A17 as a reference, or are authentication_credential_abuse and secrets the complete review scope?
